answer.html:
The strongest construction is to use a controllable correlation between two nuclear spins to select their vibrational cross spectrum. I developed a family of physical RF controls that separates the selected intramolecular contribution from same-atom and neighbouring-molecule contributions in a specified coupled-spin model. The controls and subtraction weights depend on independently measurable spin information; they do not use the mechanical force field being tested.

This is a substantive separation result, with a clear remaining boundary. It does not yet establish a usable complete-curvature measurement in a material. The unresolved requirements are retention of the pair label, calibration throughout the illuminated volume, enough prepared material, and control of the spectral tails.

There is also an important source correction: NMR-modulated neutron scattering is established prior, including work directed at selecting intra- and intermolecular correlations. The opportunity here is the specific combination of a mixed-curvature observable, physically generated contrast, and a noncircular error bound. Spin-controlled pair selection itself cannot carry the invention claim. PubMed+1

1. The quantity that survives physical separation

For a nuclear Hamiltonian

H=∑ipi22mi+V(R),H=\sum_i\frac{p_i^2}{2m_i}+V(R),H=i∑​2mi​pi2​​+V(R),

the retained observable, for distinct nuclei, is

C3,ij(q)=ℜ∫−∞∞E3Sij(q,E) dE=ℏ42mimjℜ⟨eiq⋅(Rj−Ri)qTVij′′q⟩.C_{3,ij}(q) = \Re\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}E^3S_{ij}(q,E)\,dE = \frac{\hbar^4}{2m_i m_j} \Re\left\langle e^{iq\cdot(R_j-R_i)} q^{T}V''_{ij}q \right\rangle .C3,ij​(q)=ℜ∫−∞∞​E3Sij​(q,E)dE=2mi​mj​ℏ4​ℜ⟨eiq⋅(Rj​−Ri​)qTVij′′​q⟩.

The corresponding first cross moment is zero under the stated real-potential, time-reversal-invariant mechanical assumptions.

The distinction matters: Vij′′V''_{ij}Vij′′​ differentiates with respect to the two nuclear coordinates while holding the other nuclear coordinates fixed. It can distinguish that coupling from a correlation or relaxed response transmitted through other coordinates. Electronic response already incorporated into a Born–Oppenheimer potential remains included; the result does not uniquely identify a chemical pair potential.

At finite qqq, the observable is a phase-weighted thermal mixed curvature. Independently measuring a separation distribution does not generally permit division by its structure factor:

⟨Kijeiqrij⟩≠⟨Kij⟩⟨eiqrij⟩.\langle K_{ij}e^{iqr_{ij}}\rangle \ne \langle K_{ij}\rangle\langle e^{iqr_{ij}}\rangle .⟨Kij​eiqrij​⟩=⟨Kij​⟩⟨eiqrij​⟩.

A harmonic or conditional-constancy assumption can justify that conversion in a particular model. The separation construction below does not require it.

This also preserves the earlier limitation: a first-moment null is a useful check, but it neither removes arbitrary self contamination nor certifies a complete cubic moment.

2. A molecular route to changing pair weights

For unpolarized incident neutrons, with final neutron spin unobserved, write the nuclear scattering-length operator as

bi=ai+ci σn⋅Ii.b_i=a_i+c_i\,\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{n}\cdot\mathbf I_i .bi​=ai​+ci​σn​⋅Ii​.

In the static-spin limit, its mechanical scattering weights are

Gii=ai2+ci2Ii(Ii+1),G_{ii}=a_i^2+c_i^2 I_i(I_i+1),Gii​=ai2​+ci2​Ii​(Ii​+1),

and, for distinct nuclei,

Gij=aiaj+cicj⟨Ii⋅Ij⟩.G_{ij}=a_i a_j+c_i c_j \langle\mathbf I_i\cdot\mathbf I_j\rangle .Gij​=ai​aj​+ci​cj​⟨Ii​⋅Ij​⟩.

The first expression is independent of the nuclear spin populations. The second depends on a joint spin correlation. This supplies a way to change the wanted pair weight while leaving self weights unchanged.

The stronger physical starting point I found is the parahydrogen-derived hydride pair in Ru(H)2(CO)2(dppe)\mathrm{Ru(H)_2(CO)_2(dppe)}Ru(H)2​(CO)2​(dppe). Published experiments supplied highly correlated hydride spins, resolved their two resonances, and demonstrated coherent control. The reported separation is 492 Hz and the hydride scalar coupling is 4.6 Hz; these are control parameters, not mechanical spring constants. arxiv.org

For two spin-12\tfrac1221​ nuclei, the useful stored states are

ρ−=144−αIzSz,ρ+=144+αIzSz.\rho_-=\frac{\mathbf1_4}{4}-\alpha I_zS_z, \qquad \rho_+=\frac{\mathbf1_4}{4}+\alpha I_zS_z .ρ−​=414​​−αIz​Sz​,ρ+​=414​​+αIz​Sz​.

Both have maximally mixed single-spin marginals. Their longitudinal pair correlations have opposite signs. An appropriate phase cycle followed by a selective proton inversion supplies the ideal transformation. The initial prepared state and actual pulse response must be measured.

Using the published, rounded singlet/triplet populations gives

α=0.937+0.045−0.009−0.009=0.964.\alpha =0.937+0.045-0.009-0.009 =0.964.α=0.937+0.045−0.009−0.009=0.964.

This is a source correction worth retaining: the relevant longitudinal correlation is not the paper’s approximate Werner-state purity parameter, about 0.916. The reported populations determine the contrast. arxiv.org

For independently retained molecular spin pairs,

I+(q,E)−I−(q,E)=αcH2ℜ∑ℓSHℓ,1Hℓ,2(q,E).I_+(q,E)-I_-(q,E) = \alpha c_H^2 \Re\sum_{\ell} S_{H_{\ell,1}H_{\ell,2}}(q,E).I+​(q,E)−I−​(q,E)=αcH2​ℜℓ∑​SHℓ,1​Hℓ,2​​(q,E).

Thus, in this limit:

  • Same-atom mechanical spectra cancel.
  • Pairs belonging to different molecules cancel, even when their mechanical motions are correlated.
  • The selected intramolecular pair class remains.
  • No neighbouring mechanical force is supplied or subtracted.

With the approximate scattering constants used in the calculation, the contrast coefficient is about 817 fm2817\ \mathrm{fm^2}817 fm2. Those constants are appropriate for a diagnostic calculation; an experiment would require scattering-length calibration over its actual neutron-energy band. ncnr.nist.gov

The stored states are separable. The operation does not require maintaining transverse entanglement throughout the neutron measurement.

3. I replaced the ideal inversion with a physical pulse family

A selective inversion cannot be treated as a perfect switch. I first specified a rectangular RF pulse acting on both hydrides:

  • RF Rabi frequency: 492/3=284.056492/\sqrt3=284.056492/3​=284.056 Hz.
  • Duration: 1.7601.7601.760 ms.
  • Corresponding co-rotating RF field: approximately 6.67 μT6.67\ \mu\mathrm T6.67 μT.

Without the scalar coupling, the addressed spin rotates by π\piπ, while the detuned spin makes a 2π2\pi2π rotation. I retained the measured 4.6 Hz coupling during propagation.

That finite pulse produces unwanted single-spin magnetizations. Consequently, the ideal two-setting subtraction leaves small intermolecular terms. The calculation therefore does not stop at a nominally selective pulse.

The completed family

I constructed 16 settings using the same RF amplitude and pulse durations from 0 to 7.041 ms. Each is followed by a 20 ms acquisition interval. The two-spin density matrix evolves under the same chemical-shift and scalar-coupling Hamiltonian throughout.

For each setting, the required calibration row is

(1,  ∣mA∣2‾,  ∣mB∣2‾,  mA⋅mB‾,  mAz‾,  mBz‾,  ⟨IA⋅IB⟩‾).\left( 1,\; \overline{|m_A|^2},\; \overline{|m_B|^2},\; \overline{m_A\cdot m_B},\; \overline{m_{Az}},\; \overline{m_{Bz}},\; \overline{\langle\mathbf I_A\cdot\mathbf I_B\rangle} \right).(1,∣mA​∣2​,∣mB​∣2​,mA​⋅mB​​,mAz​​,mBz​​,⟨IA​⋅IB​⟩​).

Here mAm_AmA​ and mBm_BmB​ are the measured single-spin means. The overbar denotes an acquisition-time average. Products of instantaneous means must be averaged; multiplying the averaged means gives the wrong intermolecular weights. I evaluated these averages analytically, including the frequency sums entering the quadratic terms.

The subtraction weights annihilate the first six columns and retain the desired pair-correlation column. Under the product-spin and uniform-control assumptions, this cancels the intermolecular terms for arbitrary molecular arrangements and arbitrary mechanical spectra. No spatial shell inversion is needed.

The resulting model has:

QuantityResult
Calibration rank7
Condition number after column normalizationAbout 28
Standard-deviation penalty relative to an ideal two-setting contrast, at equal raw intensity and total counts1.57
Sum of absolute subtraction weights2.679

These numbers establish that the particular physical family is not ruined by an enormous algebraic noise penalty. They do not establish the precision of experimental spin calibration. The very small nuisance columns still need appropriate absolute error bounds.

The observed molecular controls support this construction, but the published experiment did not implement these neutron-contrast settings. Its spin preparation was also dilute and required an active-volume correction. High spin purity alone does not supply a large, uniformly prepared scattering specimen. arxiv.org+1

4. A discriminating mechanical prediction from one common model

I applied the physical pulse family to a controlled mechanical model containing two H–M–H units, with explicit couplings between the units. One quadratic energy supplies all of the following:

  • The direct force derivatives.
  • The environment-mediated correlations.
  • Quantum thermal displacement statistics.
  • All-order plane-wave spectral moments.
  • Positive raw scattering intensities and their counting variance.

The model is at 295 K. Its heavy scaffold, geometry and springs are specified inputs. It is not a force-field prediction for the ruthenium complex.

The decisive comparison changes a selected direct H–H spring from zero to 0.3 eV/A˚20.3\ \mathrm{eV/\mathring A^2}0.3 eV/A˚2:

ResultNo direct H–H springDirect spring 0.3 eV/A˚20.3\ \mathrm{eV/\mathring A^2}0.3 eV/A˚2
Fixed-environment mixed Hessian000−0.300-0.300−0.300
Mixed Hessian after allowing the environment to relax−6.009-6.009−6.009−6.309-6.309−6.309
Spring recovered from the selected complete cubic momentApproximately 0000.3000.3000.300
Conditional standard error at 10910^9109 detected model counts0.02700.02700.02700.02760.02760.0276

The zero-direct-coupling case still has substantial coordinate correlation and a nonzero fifth cross moment. The selected cubic moment remains zero. This is the useful scientific discriminator: a large relaxed coupling or correlated motion need not imply a nonzero fixed-environment mixed derivative.

The counting figures include the model’s positive self-scattering noise. They exclude solvent, ligand and precursor backgrounds, prepared-product dilution, attenuation, preparation duty cycle and incomplete energy coverage. They are conditional diagnostics, not beamtime estimates or an experimental sensitivity claim.

5. The weaker routes produced two decisive failures

Species contrast removes self terms but leaves a difficult neighbouring-pair problem

Independent H/D polarization reversal can isolate an H–D cross spectrum. It retains every H–D pair, so a subsequent separation is still necessary.

In the common four-atom model, the spatial inversion was well conditioned. Nevertheless, recovering an intermolecular spring of 0.08 eV/A˚20.08\ \mathrm{eV/\mathring A^2}0.08 eV/A˚2 to 10% required approximately 3.2×10153.2\times10^{15}3.2×1015 detected model counts. The strong molecular vibration dominated the sixth-moment counting variance.

I also retained the control failure: an apparently reasonable four-state reversal cycle with equal 10% polarization loss had rank three and did not identify the desired cross term. A longer calibrated trajectory restored identification. Calling four acquisitions “four contrasts” was insufficient.

A clean contrast can still produce a false curvature through spectral truncation

Using the same mechanical Hamiltonian and its complete multiphonon spectrum:

Treatment of the spectrumRecovered intermolecular spring
Complete spectrum0.080 eV/A˚20.080\ \mathrm{eV/\mathring A^2}0.080 eV/A˚2
Truncate at 1 eV and ignore the missing partApproximately 2.00 eV/A˚22.00\ \mathrm{eV/\mathring A^2}2.00 eV/A˚2

This failure is much larger than the target. It survives excellent contrast conditioning.

Nor does an incident neutron energy of 2 eV provide a 2 eV loss window at every momentum transfer. The kinematic boundary is

Emax⁡(q,Ei)=2ℏ22mnEi q−ℏ2q22mn.E_{\max}(q,E_i) = 2\sqrt{\frac{\hbar^2}{2m_n}E_i}\,q -\frac{\hbar^2q^2}{2m_n}.Emax​(q,Ei​)=22mn​ℏ2​Ei​​q−2mn​ℏ2q2​.

Published low-angle, high-energy neutron instrumentation is relevant evidence, but its existence does not acquire arbitrary q,Eq,Eq,E coverage or the combined molecular-control experiment. art.torvergata.it

The dilute-HD pair-tag route also has a scoped failure. A recent solid-parahydrogen experiment supplies a resolved HD spin coupling and an attractive millisecond gate timescale. At its demonstrated 4 K and approximately 1.4 T conditions, however, the calculated thermal proton polarization is only 3.6×10−43.6\times10^{-4}3.6×10−4. The high polarizations of dense frozen-HD targets cannot be imported into that dilute coherent specimen without additional construction. arxiv.org

That is why the parahydrogen-derived hydride pair became the stronger actuator candidate.

6. Calibration can bound contamination without supplying the force field

The useful completion is an error bound tied to observable quantities.

Let TTT denote the desired pair selector. Suppose independent spin and beam calibration gives

∑kwkGk=D T+R,\sum_k w_kG_k=D\,T+R,k∑​wk​Gk​=DT+R,

where RRR is the residual unwanted scattering-weight matrix.

For a positive reference matrix GrefG_{\rm ref}Gref​, constructed from acquired settings, define

η=∥Gref−1/2R Gref−1/2∥op.\eta= \left\| G_{\rm ref}^{-1/2}R\,G_{\rm ref}^{-1/2} \right\|_{\rm op}.η=​Gref−1/2​RGref−1/2​​op​.

Because the mechanical spectral matrix is positive,

∣Tr⁡(RS)∣≤η Tr⁡(GrefS)=ηIref.|\operatorname{Tr}(RS)| \le \eta\,\operatorname{Tr}(G_{\rm ref}S) = \eta I_{\rm ref}.∣Tr(RS)∣≤ηTr(Gref​S)=ηIref​.

Over a measured energy window WWW,

∣δC3W∣≤η∣D∣∫W∣E∣3Iref(q,E) dE.|\delta C_3^W| \le \frac{\eta}{|D|} \int_W |E|^3I_{\rm ref}(q,E)\,dE .∣δC3W​∣≤∣D∣η​∫W​∣E∣3Iref​(q,E)dE.

The unknown mechanical interaction does not enter this certificate. The ingredients are an independently bounded contrast error and a measured positive reference spectrum.

There are three qualifications that materially change whether the certificate is useful.

First, local spin calibration is not automatically a calibration of the neighbouring-pair weights. I constructed an explicit counterexample: an ensemble of

∣↑↓↑↓⟩and∣↓↑↓↑⟩|\uparrow\downarrow\uparrow\downarrow\rangle \quad\text{and}\quad |\downarrow\uparrow\downarrow\uparrow\rangle∣↑↓↑↓⟩and∣↓↑↓↑⟩

has the same local anticorrelated pair populations as independently prepared pairs, but carries an unwanted inter-molecular correlation

⟨I1zI4z⟩=−14.\langle I_{1z}I_{4z}\rangle=-\frac14.⟨I1z​I4z​⟩=−41​.

Thus, even perfect longitudinal pair-population measurements do not prove that the labels remain confined to their original molecules. Preparation from independent pairs and subsequent spin or chemical exchange must be independently controlled or bounded. The measured T1T_1T1​ and T2T_2T2​ values alone do not establish that retention.

Second, spatially averaged polarization is insufficient. Different RF fields, preparation ages or photochemical populations across the sample can produce different products of local means. The actual calibration must describe the neutron-visible volume, or bound those variations. A small two-molecule residual cannot simply be declared a bulk bound.

Third, spectral tails require their own information. For an unmeasured tail T\mathcal TT,

∣∫TE3ℜSAB dE∣≤∫T∣E∣3SAA dE  ∫T∣E∣3SBB dE.\left|\int_{\mathcal T}E^3\Re S_{AB}\,dE\right| \le \sqrt{ \int_{\mathcal T}|E|^3S_{AA}\,dE\; \int_{\mathcal T}|E|^3S_{BB}\,dE }.​∫T​E3ℜSAB​dE​≤∫T​∣E∣3SAA​dE∫T​∣E∣3SBB​dE​.

The positive tails must themselves be measured or independently bounded. Computing them from the force field under test would reintroduce circularity.

I also included nuclear-spin energy shifts explicitly for the ideal stored pair states. Equal static self weights do not guarantee identical energy-resolved self spectra. Those corrections can be calculated from independently acquired spin energies and populations and bounded using lower mechanical moments. Coordinate dependence of the spin Hamiltonian—such as J(R)J(R)J(R)—is a separate term; a small measured JJJ is not, by itself, a bound on its derivatives.

7. What the strongest alternatives already provide

The comparison becomes more precise once all methods receive the same structural and calibration information.

AlternativeWhat it already suppliesRemaining role for this construction
Coherent vibrational spectroscopyInterference-sensitive measurements have determined phonon eigenvector phases. Complete mode energies and eigenvectors determine a harmonic Hessian.A different physical route to a selected pair’s cross spectrum when full environmental mode reconstruction is impractical. If spectroscopy supplies that same spectrum, it supplies the same moment information.
NMR-modulated neutron scatteringThe direct prior for nuclear-spin-controlled partial scattering and intra/intermolecular selection.The specific force observable, explicit nuisance cancellation and usable error budget must justify further work.
NRIXS and neutron-Compton reconstructionEstablished moment and potential-reconstruction methods already provide force-related and anharmonic information.A selected mixed derivative is a different target from an on-site projection or one-coordinate effective potential.
Force reconstruction and interventionsFull harmonic information can recover forces; physically accessible coordinates can be manipulated and their interactions measured.The proposed operation matters where the wanted nuclear pair cannot be independently displaced and read while the environment is held fixed.

The comparison becomes more precise once all methods receive the same structural and calibration information.

Alternative	What it already supplies	Remaining role for this construction
Coherent vibrational spectroscopy	Interference-sensitive measurements have determined phonon eigenvector phases. Complete mode energies and eigenvectors determine a harmonic Hessian. Force reconstruction and interventions	Full harmonic information can recover forces; physically accessible coordinates can be manipulated and their interactions measured.	The proposed operation matters where the wanted nuclear pair cannot be independently displaced and read while the environment is held fixed.

Scientific decision

I would retain the calibrated molecular-pair contrast construction and the direct-versus-relaxed force discriminator as the main opening. They move the branch beyond overlapping illumination: the selector now has an actual molecular control mechanism, finite pulse dynamics, explicit nuisance columns and a noncircular contamination bound.

The present ruthenium experiment supplies strong spin-control evidence, but not a demonstrated usable neutron specimen. The next decisive material information is the absolute amount and lifetime of retained pair order, including transfer to neighbouring molecules, together with the positive spectral weight needed to certify the cubic moment. Further pulse or spatial-grid refinement cannot substitute for those quantities.

The proofs, complete executable calculations, reconstructed identifiability example, reported electron-mask failure, and new failures are preserved in
